rules.statement: a. Each citation names a SOURCE block's id, copies one `locator=` value from that block exactly (for example page:1: no brackets, ranges or notes) and quotes a verbatim substring of that span's text. Runs of whitespace and line breaks may be written as one space and curly quotes or dashes in ASCII; every other character is copied exactly, and the quote must be in the span its locator names. Copy a run that is contiguous in the SOURCE block as printed; never reassemble a sentence across interleaved table text. Never continue a quote onto the next page.

b. Quotes appear only in `market_evidence`: each observed or indicative_talk row quotes one span of a source listed under `market_evidence_sources` in the CONTEXT block, its `quote.source_id` equal to its `source_id`, one row per quoted span. A `none` row quotes nothing (a null `quote`) and states its `limitation`. A `basis` refers to Python's context rows by id (`basis.context_rows`) and never copies their figures; a `basis.quotes` entry still repeats a `market_evidence` row's quote exactly, for the rows of a `third_party` source only.

c. Indicative talk is never a market level: an `observed` row never quotes talk wording (talk, indicative, guidance, initial price thoughts), and neither an indicative_talk row's own text nor a text whose basis is talk alone uses a level verb (trades at, quoted at, priced at, yields). With talk only, the preference's `confidence` is below High.

d. Name instruments only by a `facility_id` listed under `cp1_facilities`, each once. Every instrument and risk has a basis: its `cp2_refs` (only refs listed under `cp2_rows`), a `{ref|unit}` CP-1 figure or, for an instrument, a `basis.quotes` market quote or a context row named in `basis.context_rows`; a `market_observation` other than none cites a market quote or a context row named in `basis.context_rows`.

e. `preference.ordering` lists every instrument's `facility_id` exactly once and nothing else: you may order the issuer's own instruments, most preferred first. Unless its `confidence` is Insufficient Information it cites a market quote or a context row named in `basis.context_rows`; with no observed or indicative evidence it is Insufficient Information and states its `limitation`. Its `confidence` is below High while `confidence_caps` lists any cap.
f. Every text field is nonblank run text: labels only; a figure only as `{ref|unit}` from `cp1_facts` or inside a verbatim quote; never a bare number or a `[ref]` chip.

g. No instrument action, peer ranking or recovery conclusion in any text field: never buy, sell, overweight, underweight, recommend or switch into or out of an instrument, never rank the issuer against peers and never state an expected recovery; an intra-issuer preference (preferred, prefer the term loan) is allowed.
